description: POST-HOC analyses (not pre-registered) of event dependence (A, B) and of the forward regressions under the study's own oracles (C, D); produced by scripts/revision_dependence.py. Inputs are only read. A/B use the 19 scale-up mutation events (data_scaleup/); C/D use results/forward_units/*_v2(.corrected).json.

conventions.holm: within the 3 comparisons of one analysis variant
conventions.bootstrap: percentile, 5000 resamples, numpy default_rng(0) fresh per quantity

definitions.detection_set: units u with detects[u] True in _build_payloads(data_scaleup)
definitions.jaccard: |S∩T|/|S∪T|; two empty sets are identical, Jaccard := 1
definitions.clusters: connected components (single linkage) of the Jaccard >= 0.8 graph

eigen_based.note: phi (Pearson) correlation of the non-constant columns; constant columns (events no unit detects) have no correlation and are excluded, then counted as `n_constant_column_groups` distinct pattern(s)

B_dependence_robustness.difference: r4(a) - r4(b) per event; positive = a better (higher AUC)

tests.wilcoxon: two-sided, zero_method='wilcox', method='auto' (scipy), on r4 values
tests.sign_test: exact two-sided binomial on wins vs losses (ties dropped)
tests.permutation: paired sign-flip of the nonzero r4 differences, statistic |sum|, exact when <= 20 nonzero
tests.holm3: Holm within the 3 comparisons of the same analysis variant
tests.cluster_bootstrap: percentile, Jaccard>=0.8 clusters (within the analysed subset) resampled with replacement, event-weighted mean of the drawn clusters, 5000, default_rng(0) fresh per quantity

i_dedup_identical_alphabetical_first.rule: keep the alphabetically first event of each identical-detection-set group

ii_cluster_level.note: cluster-bootstrap intervals are reported in each variant's results (cluster_bootstrap_ci95). Here, additionally, each Jaccard>=0.8 cluster is collapsed to the mean of its events' r4 AUCs and the tests are run across clusters (cluster means are not re-rounded; ties are exact equality of cluster means).

replication.quality: cart.oracles.quality.evaluate_quality is called unchanged with thresholds QualityThresholds.load(configs/thresholds.yaml) ({'tau_2q': 0.1, 'tau_depth': 0.1, 'tau_depth_improve': 0.1, 'tau_2q_improve': 0.1}) on duck-typed stand-ins: count_2q(stand-in) returns the stored n2q and .depth() the stored depth. A hand re-implementation of rules 1/2 is run alongside and must agree on every unit.
replication.quality_assumption: stored n2q = count of {cx, cz, ecr, swap} ops of the transpiled output (scripts/forward_probe_units.py), whereas count_2q counts every 2-qubit op except barrier. With basis_gates [cx, rz, sx, x] the outputs contain no other 2-qubit op, so the two coincide; this cannot be re-checked without the circuits. Stored depth = QuantumCircuit.depth(), as in evaluate_quality.
replication.performance: cart.oracles.performance.screen_performance(baseline_times, candidate_times, slowdown_threshold=0.2) (performance.stage1_slowdown_threshold of configs/thresholds.yaml). Primary: one-element lists holding the FIRST wall-clock run of each build (cf. historical_runner.run_historical_event, which screens one cold run per build in a fresh subprocess). Sensitivity: median of all runs (wall), and the first CPU-process-time run (the instrument historical_worker records; 15.6 ms resolution on Windows, and screen_performance returns ratio 0 when the baseline time is 0).
replication.not_replicable: the semantic/functional oracles (and their precedence over quality/performance in the label hierarchy) need the circuits, which are not stored; 'flagged' therefore means quality regression OR performance screen, and the label precedence quality > performance is applied only to name the label.
replication.detection_for_selectors: pipeline_first = quality OR first-run wall screen (primary); pipeline_median = quality OR median wall screen; also quality-only and screen-only
replication.selector_eval: as scripts/forward_selector_eval.py with --clock wall: cost = median candidate wall time + ORACLE_COST_EST[oracle_type] (0.05 default); baseline_costs = median baseline wall time; history = []; ctx units = the 116 usable units; ranking with SELECTORS_SCALEUP at an infinite budget, seed 0 (random: mean over seeds 0..19); tests_to_first_detection = 1-based position of the first detecting unit, len(ranking)+1 if none. The budget-tier (pr/nightly) part of that script is not repeated.

label_matched_detection.note: number of units whose pipeline label (first-run screen) equals cart.labels.ground_truth.LABEL_FOR_FAULT[fault_type], i.e. the study's own fault_id_detected rule; quality/performance labels cannot match a contract_metadata event

fwd-applylayout-registers-14904.selectors_note: per detection definition; an AUC of 0 and tests_to_first_detection = n_units+1 mean no unit is flagged

hist-vf2postlayout-noop.fault_matched_rule: median wall ratio >= 1.5 and difference >= 0.01 s

hist-vf2postlayout-noop.selectors_note: per detection definition; an AUC of 0 and tests_to_first_detection = n_units+1 mean no unit is flagged

fwd-applylayout-registers-14904.role: supplementary (contract event; only 2 runs per build)

hist-vf2postlayout-noop.role: PRIMARY (performance event, last-good build a18e151 after the documented baseline/candidate label correction)

D_single_run_screen_false_alarms.definition: 'a->b' = number of units flagged by screen_performance([run a], [run b], 0.20), run a in the baseline role and run b in the candidate role, both runs from the SAME build; any flag is a false alarm. Rates are per unit (/n_units). Run 1 of every unit is the first transpile in a fresh process (cold), so pairs with run 1 mix a warm-up effect into the comparison; 'excluding run 1' uses only warm runs. The cold-vs-cold comparison that the primary first-run screen of section C makes cannot be reproduced within one build (one cold run per unit and build).
